title: Sunday Morning
subtitle: A mother exits the cotton field, her son becomes an "outlaw."

items.text: A Fool's Gold
Sunday Morning
Sunday morning.
Everything suggests that today is set to be a fine one.
The eastern wind brings wisps of white pampas grass, mingling with the city crowds, infusing the streets with a spirit of quiet contentment.
That is until the first fuel drum explodes.
The Headonion Show

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Earlier this morning, two suspects made a daring escape from a blazing gas station, their van driving away at breakneck speeds.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Eyewitness reports identify them as the same suspects who have brazenly attacked over half of the city's gas stations previously.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: This is ONiON—first on the ground and live at the scene. Through rigorous investigation, our team is committed to uncovering the truth of this case, one clue at a time.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: In fact, our initial findings have revealed this explosion to be merely the prelude to a far more complex tale.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: The common thread weaving through this story is a name—

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: something that has stood as the ultimate hope for all, the muse that has sparked the soul of inspiration for millennia.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: It is the true value of gold:
MacGuffin the Knife.
Lobby, Suitcase

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: They usually stay around three to eight inches from your body.
The world outside may turn, but in the suitcase, life is steady—organically stable, perpetually still.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Some are sweet like honey, while others taste like iron.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Oh, and the wick is something else too, warming the tongue without getting too spicy.
In the common room, they form a circle, hand-in-hand with eyes closed. A flame comes alive in the center, and gray smoke lifts into the air.
"Communing with one's own spirit," that's one interpretation of this ritual.
Mercuria navigates the spiritual items, aromatic herbs, and candles on the floor, pausing behind each individual.
She strikes the singing bowl, then rubs rosemary behind the ears of each participant.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Trauma lingers like a taste ... a ringing in the ears, sour, slightly bitter, yet ... refreshing.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Argus's eyebrows draw together, reflecting her discomfort.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Parchment ... the hum of static and leather. Fascinating—oh, good.
ONiON's head shakes, then promptly settles back into a state of calmness.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: A gust from a painting, earthy and heavy. Painful, but passing.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Druvis inhales softly, her features smooth and serene.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Meadows, sweat-soaked medals, the logic of brown, and ... sunlit pages.
Dogs often have a higher body temperature than people, especially the more intelligent varieties.
Mercuria extends her hand, her fingers dancing above Pickles's head as if tapping piano keys.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Good, now everything's in order.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof, woof ...

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof ... woof ... woof, woof, woof ...

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Grrr ...

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: I like the aura of your thoughts; their shine has such a unique hue.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof?

items.speaker: "Doggie"
items.text: The puppy is surprised.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Surprised, yes, but curious—even more so.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Your translator is not as precise as it should be.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof-woof, woof, woof, woof ... woof.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof, woof, woof ... woof, woof, woof.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Aroo, woof, woof, woof.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Thanks for noticing.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Perhaps someday, we'll get to know each other better.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: It appears our healer has discovered a technique for communicating with animals.
Druvis offers a summary of their interaction.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Mercuria, I have a letter for you.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Oh! What are you all up to?
The meticulous girl, laden with letters and documents, stumbles into the impromptu gathering.
Before anyone has a chance to respond, the smoke detector above reaches its limit, overloaded like lungs inhaling too much smoke.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Oh, what a delightful rain.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: We may need to upgrade the smoke alarm system in the common room to prevent it from being "excessively responsive" during these ceremonies.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: The spirits are grateful.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Miss Mercuria, I have your mail—
She offers the letter outward.
Mercuria reaches for it, only to hesitate and retract her hand.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Ominous berries, like the ones you find in a bog.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Is everything alright? The canteen has been swamped with letters just like it. They've been putting a burden on our operations.
Still hesitant, Mercuria takes the letter, quietly smooths it out, and begins to read.
She reads with the utmost seriousness—slowly, very—slowly ...
Until at last, she folds the letter and prepares to leave.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Oh, just a moment, please—
Mercuria's steps are natural and steady, and doesn't slow a moment against her words.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What's the matter? Is there something going on? Please, Ms. Mercuria, you can tell me.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: My friend.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Panic, like fresh currants and seedless apples.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Are you talking about his energy?

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: He needs me.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: So, you intend to find him and help regulate his energy? Is that what this is all about?

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: But ...
After wringing out her wet coat, the journalist edges nearer.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: That letterhead, it's definitely not store-bought.
A white-gloved hand makes contact with the letter, turning it over.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Take a look.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Texas State Penitentiary at Huntsville?
The eyes of all present move from the envelope to Mercuria's face, but she betrays no hint of emotion beyond her calm determination.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Yes, that's his address.
